front: EKS VPC CNI in one sentence (and its main risk)
back: Pods get real VPC IPs from your subnets; the risk is IP exhaustion, mitigated with bigger/secondary CIDRs, prefix delegation or IPv6.

Managed node groups (default), self-managed nodes, Fargate (pod per micro-VM, no DaemonSets), Karpenter (just-in-time right-sized nodes, consolidation), EKS Auto Mode (AWS-managed compute and core add-ons).

front: EKS: how do IAM principals get cluster access today?
back: Access entries (EKS API) with access policies or Kubernetes groups bound via RBAC. The `aws-auth` ConfigMap is the deprecated older method.
Control plane upgrades one minor at a time. kubelet never newer than the API server, up to 3 minors older. kubectl within ±1 minor.

front: PDB setting that never blocks drains (with ≥2 replicas)
back: `maxUnavailable: 1`, with replicas spread across nodes and readiness probes so replacements count as available.
